newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai ups commercial vehicle capacity.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai ups commercial vehicle capacity.

text.p: South Korea's largest carmaker Hyundai Motor Co began full operation of its new commerical vehicle plant with an annual production capacity of 100,000 units, a company statement said on Thursday.
The company said the plant, located in the southwestern city of Chonju, was the world's largest single commerical vehicle plant.
Hyundai Motor, flagship unit of the Hyundai Group, produced 250,000 commercial vehicles last year in its existing plants in southeastern city of Ulsan.
Hyundai invested 370 billion won to build the Chonju plant, which has a capacity to produce 18,000 large buses and 82,000 trucks, bulk cement trailers and oil tanker trucks.
The statement quoted company president Park Byung-jae as saying the company would actively market in Asia, the Middle East, Latin America and Europe with the commerical vehicles.

"Hyundai plans to export 50 percent of the factory's output, or about 50,000 commerical vehicles, in the year 2000," Park said. He said the new plant would create 10,000 new jobs and contribute to adding 1.7 trillion won in annual sales.
